why: Item 1: one expect line asks for a README heading for every function index.js exports: "Every function exported by index.js has its own `## name(` heading... capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft". It names slugify, so the README check covers more than padLeft. Its proof script compares the exports against the README headings. Item 2: the expect lines pin what padLeft does both with and without a fill character. With a fill: "padLeft('42', 5, '0') returns '00042'" and "padLeft(42, 5, '0')... returns the string '00042'". With no fill: "padLeft('42', 5) returns '   42'". So the 42 -> 00042 padding can be checked, and each of these lines has a run proof. Both items are handled.
